Om Prakash Agrawal And Another vs State Of Up And 3 Others
on 12 November, 2024

Author: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
Bench: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:177022-Db
Court No. - 42
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 13485 of 2024
Petitioner :- Om Prakash Agrawal And Another
Respondent :- State Of Up And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Amit Daga,Krishna Mohan Garg

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- Arun Kumar Yadav,G.A.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.
Heard Sri K.M. Garg, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Arun Kumar Yadav, learned counsel appearing for the informant and Sri G.P. Singh, learned A.G.A.-1 appearing for the State respondents.

2. This writ petition has been filed praying to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 10-07-2024, registered as FIR No. 352 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Prem Nagar, District Jhansi.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 24-09-2024 had referred the matter to the mediation centre.

4. Perused the office report dated 12-11-2024 and the settlement agreement dated 26-10-2024 which indicates that matter has been peacefully settled between the parties and they have settled their differences on the terms mentioned in paragraph 7 of the settlement agreement dated 11.4.2023.

The paragraph 7 is quoted as under:-
"7. The following settlement has been arrived at between the parties hereto:-
a) That both the parties have amicably resolved their dispute out side the Court and in this regard on 21.09.2024, the Respondent No.4 has executed sale deed of the disputed land in favour of Petitioners.

A Razinama signed by both the parties has already been filed in Civil Suit No.174 of 2024, before the Civil Judge, (JD), Jhansi.
The copy of the said Razinama is being annexed to this settlement for kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.
b) That both the parties reiterate and reaffirm the terms and conditions mentioned in the Razinama.
c) That both the parties undertake that they do not want to litigate further as all the disputes and differences have been resolved between them.

d) That it has been agreed between the parties that the Respondent No.4 shall have no objection in any manner whatsoever, if the Hon'ble Court pleases to allow the present Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13485 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13485 of 2024

sentences.text: e) That it has also been agreed between the parties all the cases of civil or criminal nature, if any, pending against each other regarding present dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the concerned Authorities in view of this settlement-agreement.
(f) That both the parties have finally agreed that in pursuance to the present final settlement they will not file any fresh cases against each other in respect of the present dispute in future also.
g) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse.
h. That this settlement has been read over and explained to the parties in Hindi in presence of their respective counsels and thereafter they have signed this settlement."

6. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana), J.T. 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of investigation and another), (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab),
(2014) 9 SCC 653 (Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also (2014) 6 SCC 466 (Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab) and in view of the settlement agreement dated 26-10-2024,
the impugned First Information Report dated 10-07-2024, registered as FIR No. 352 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Prem Nagar, District Jhansi is hereby quashed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 24-09-2024 had referred the matter to the mediation centre.
4. Perused the office report dated 12-11-2024 and the settlement agreement dated 26-10-2024 which indicates that matter has been peacefully settled between the parties and they have settled their differences on the terms mentioned in paragraph 7 of the settlement agreement dated 11.4.2023.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The paragraph 7 is quoted as under:-
"7. The following settlement has been arrived at between the parties hereto:-
a) That both the parties have amicably resolved their dispute out side the Court and in this regard on 21.09.2024, the Respondent No.4 has executed sale deed of the disputed land in favour of Petitioners.
A Razinama signed by both the parties has already been filed in Civil Suit No.174 of 2024, before the Civil Judge, (JD), Jhansi.
The copy of the said Razinama is being annexed to this settlement for kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.
b) That both the parties reiterate and reaffirm the terms and conditions mentioned in the Razinama.
c) That both the parties undertake that they do not want to litigate further as all the disputes and differences have been resolved between them.
d) That it has been agreed between the parties that the Respondent No.4 shall have no objection in any manner whatsoever, if the Hon'ble Court pleases to allow the present Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13485 of 2024.
e) That it has also been agreed between the parties all the cases of civil or criminal nature, if any, pending against each other regarding present dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the concerned Authorities in view of this settlement-agreement.
(f) That both the parties have finally agreed that in pursuance to the present final settlement they will not file any fresh cases against each other in respect of the present dispute in future also.
g) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse.
h. That this settlement has been read over and explained to the parties in Hindi in presence of their respective counsels and thereafter they have signed this settlement."
It is submitted that as between the parties compromise had already taken place therefore, the impugned First Information Report dated 10-07-2024, registered as FIR No. 352 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Prem Nagar, District Jhansi is liable to be quashed.
7. The present petition is, accordingly, allowed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
6. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana), J.T. 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of investigation and another), (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab),
(2014) 9 SCC 653 (Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also (2014) 6 SCC 466 (Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab) and in view of the settlement agreement dated 26-10-2024,
the impugned First Information Report dated 10-07-2024, registered as FIR No. 352 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Prem Nagar, District Jhansi is hereby quashed.
